Subject: Inference economics & SLO tiering — BrightOps discovery recap and next steps

Sara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a handful of concrete asks so we can turn this into a short proposal: 

Call summary (high level)
- Primary use case: customer-facing conversational assistant for billing & ops help; heavy short-turnaround queries with occasional long context.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~12M tokens / month.
- Peak concurrent QPS: ~55-65 qps with short bursts to 100 qps.
- Latency target (customer goal): p95 <= 250 ms for the high-priority route. Some lower-priority flows can tolerate p95 ~500 ms.

Cost & unit economics context
- You're aiming for an operational target ~$700–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on latency SLO and whether streaming is required.
- Two clear knobs: streaming (lower latency, higher cost) vs batching (better $/token at higher p95). Also model choice and quantization will move the needle.

Routing/SLO options we discussed
- SLO-driven tiers: Route critical user queries to a streaming low-latency tier (reserved capacity / dedicated) and bulk or async queries to a batched lower-cost tier (hosted or burst).
- Fallbacks: can route to a lower-cost compatible model if dedicated capacity is saturated.

Asks / next steps (please reply inline)
1) Confirm monthly token estimate (12M assumed) and peak QPS/burst profile (you mentioned 55–65 qps steady bursts).
2) Confirm desired p95 for the high-priority route (250 ms?) and for lower-priority flows.
3) Provide a rough monthly budget range (you mentioned $X–$Y / 1M tokens on the call — can you confirm the target $/1M tokens we should bake into the proposal?).

We attached the MA qualification spreadsheet that we used to capture the metrics during the call — please fill the green row (traffic mix) if you want us to produce a sample cost projection.

I'll coordinate with Marissa and Priyom on an SLO-driven pricing sketch and a short proposal with 2 options: (A) low-latency streaming path with dedicated capacity; (B) mixed-tier with batched hosted + canary low-latency path.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sync early next week to review the numbers and pick a path. What times on Monday/Tuesday morning (PST) work for you?

Thanks,

Nice recap, Rachel — listing a couple of pragmatic price bands and what they imply for architecture. See attached pricing-model-v2.csv for the quick calc.

Assumptions used (back-of-envelope)
- Model baseline: open LLM quantized to int8 runtime; streaming has ~1.6x CPU/GPU util per token vs batched execution.
- Effective tokens/month: 12M (as confirmed).
- Peak shaping: assume we provision for sustained 65 qps and allow burst autoscaling.

Representative unit economics (rounded)
- Low-latency streaming tier (p95 <= 250 ms, reserved/dedicated): ~$1,050 per 1M tokens (includes reserved GPU cost amortized + GPU ops + networking).
- Hybrid SLO (stream critical flows; batch less-critical): blended ~$850 per 1M tokens (critical 20% of tokens at streaming rates, 80% batched).
- Batched-only (p95 target ~500 ms, hosted autoscale): ~$520 per 1M tokens (best-effort batching + cheaper model variant).

Notes and tradeoffs
- If BrightOps can accept a 20% tier for critical queries (smaller fraction), the blended $/1M hits the ~$800–$1,000 target you listed without fully committing to dedicated fleet.
- If true 250ms p95 is non-negotiable for >50% of queries, the dedicated streaming path is the safer predictability route.

Next actions I recommend
1) Produce 3-line proposal (Rachel) with the above three options and high-level cost math.
2) Engineering check (Priyom) on any constraints for hooking into BrightOps' existing telemetry for request routing (SLO routing keys).
3) If BrightOps agrees to the blended pattern, we draft canary & rollout plan (1 month pilot, 80/20 traffic split).

HubSpot: I added notes to company record BR-2027-421 and attached the calc.
